helpCenter.title: Help Center
helpCenter.pathMark.whatIs.headline: Teach Bakabase to understand your existing folder structure
helpCenter.pathMark.whatIs.intro: You don't need to reorganize your files for Bakabase. Path marks are rules applied to file paths: they read your existing directory structure, automatically identify resources, fill in property values, and assign resources to media libraries. How you arrange your folders is entirely up to you.
helpCenter.pathMark.whatIs.diagram.resul: Both assigned to the "Movies" media library
You can then filter by "Genre" and browse by media library on the resource page.
helpCenter.pathMark.whatIs.markTypes.res: Decides which files or folders are "resources" — the basic unit Bakabase manages. Match by layer or regex, at any depth.
helpCenter.pathMark.whatIs.markTypes.pro: Automatically fills property values (tags, categories, authors, ...) for matched resources. Values can be fixed or dynamically extracted from the path.
helpCenter.pathMark.whatIs.markTypes.med: Assigns matched resources to a media library. Libraries can also be created dynamically from directory names.
helpCenter.pathMark.whatIs.markTypes.res: Resource marks are the foundation of everything: only paths matched by a resource mark become resources. Property marks and media library marks only take effect on existing resources.
helpCenter.pathMark.whatIs.workflow.step: Find the folder you want to manage in the directory tree.
Right-click or use "Add Mark", configure the matching rule, and preview affected paths live.
Sync reads your marks and generates resources, property values, and media library associations.
helpCenter.pathMark.whatIs.workflow.sync: Auto-sync is on by default and runs after mark changes; you can disable it in settings and trigger sync manually via "Pending Sync".
helpCenter.pathMark.examples.intro: Each example shows the folder structure, the marks to add, and the result after sync. Colors match mark types: green = resource, blue = property, purple = media library.
Movie collection basics: one folder per movie
The most common structure: each subfolder under the movie root holds one movie.
Resource mark: layer = 1 — each subfolder under the root becomes a resource.
Media library mark: fixed to the "Movies" library, scope includes subdirectories.
"Interstellar" and "Inception" become resources and show up in the "Movies" library.
Movie library with a genre level
An extra genre level in between? Resources can live at any depth, and the middle level can become a property.
Resource mark: layer = 2 — second-level subfolders become resources.
Property mark: property "Genre", value dynamically taken from the layer-1 folder name.
Resources automatically get "Genre = Sci-Fi / Drama" without manual input, ready for filtering.
helpCenter.pathMark.examples.animeSeason: Anime archived by season — the season folder name becomes a property value directly.
Resource mark: layer = 2 — each show's folder is one resource.
Property mark: property "Season", value dynamically taken from the layer-1 folder name (e.g. 2024-04).
Just create one folder per season — the season property is generated automatically.
helpCenter.pathMark.examples.mangaAuthor: Folder names like "[Author] Title"? Use a regex to extract the author into a property.
Resource mark: layer = 1 — each title folder is one resource.
Property mark: property "Author", value extracted from the folder name with regex \[(.+?)\].
Author properties are filled automatically — open an author to see all their works.
helpCenter.pathMark.examples.musicLibrar: Album folders are resources; the artist folder above them becomes a property.
Resource mark: layer = 2 — each album folder is one resource.
Property mark: property "Artist", value dynamically taken from the layer-1 folder name.
Browse albums by artist; the same idea applies to any "person / work" structure.
helpCenter.pathMark.examples.autoLibrari: Don't want to create libraries manually? Let layer-1 folder names decide the library.
Media library mark: dynamic mode — the layer-1 folder name becomes the library name, auto-created if missing.
Resource mark: layer = 2 — recognizes the content under each library.
Creating a new top-level folder equals creating a new media library — zero extra configuration.
One file tree, multiple stacked marks
The same resource can match several marks at once — each takes effect independently.
Property mark: fixed "Status = Ongoing", scope includes subdirectories.
Property mark: "Season" dynamically taken from the folder name.
"Frieren" gets its library, status, and season all at once; use priority to control processing order when marks interact.
helpCenter.pathMark.examples.extensionFi: Subtitles, posters, and metadata files mixed in? Use file type filtering to pick out the main video.
Resource mark: layer = 2 + files only + restrict to video extensions (extension groups supported).
Only movie.mkv becomes a resource — srt / jpg / nfo files stay out of the resource list.
helpCenter.pathMark.examples.resourceBou: The internals of disc rips and other self-contained folders shouldn't be split into more resources.
The whole disc folder is one resource; its internal BDMV / STREAM structure is never scanned further.
helpCenter.pathMark.examples.scopeTag.ti: Tag an entire folder at once
helpCenter.pathMark.examples.scopeTag.de: Give every resource under the "Completed" folder the same status without touching them one by one.
helpCenter.pathMark.examples.scopeTag.ma: Property mark: fixed "Status = Completed", apply scope = matched item and subdirectories.
helpCenter.pathMark.examples.scopeTag.re: Works moved into the "Completed" folder get the status automatically; move them out and re-sync to update.
helpCenter.pathMark.examples.scheduledSy: For folders that keep receiving new content, let the mark re-sync on a schedule.
Resource mark: layer = 1 + "scheduled sync" enabled (e.g. hourly).
Newly downloaded content becomes resources at the next scheduled sync — no manual steps.
helpCenter.pathMark.examples.keepIdentit: Renamed or moved a resource folder? Ratings, properties, and play history survive.
No new mark needed: enable "Keep resource identity" in the path mark settings.
Bakabase writes a bakabase.json identity file into each resource folder; after the path changes, re-sync finds the original resource and updates its path.
helpCenter.pathMark.comparison.intro: Compared with the two common approaches, path marks decouple "how files are arranged" from "how data is managed": rules describe the structure, and data is generated automatically.
helpCenter.pathMark.comparison.row.noRes: No required directory layout — no moving or renaming files
helpCenter.pathMark.comparison.row.anyLe: Resources at any depth (even mixed depths in one tree)
helpCenter.pathMark.comparison.row.dynam: Property values extracted from paths (layer / regex capture)
Media libraries auto-created from folder names
helpCenter.pathMark.comparison.row.stack: Multiple rule sets stacked on the same files
helpCenter.pathMark.comparison.row.previ: Preview affected paths before rules take effect
helpCenter.pathMark.comparison.row.anyFi: Any media type (video, manga, music, arbitrary files)
helpCenter.pathMark.comparison.row.porta: Rules can be copied, pasted, and migrated in bulk
helpCenter.pathMark.comparison.note: "Scraper-style media manager" refers broadly to tools that require a fixed directory convention and focus on metadata scraping; "manual tagging tool" refers to tools where entries and tags are maintained by hand. Individual products vary — this table summarizes typical behavior.
helpCenter.pathMark.concept.layer.name: Layer
helpCenter.pathMark.concept.layer.long: Layers are counted from the selected path: 0 = the selected path itself, 1 = its direct children, and so on. Layer = 1 means "every subfolder / file directly under the selected directory".
helpCenter.pathMark.concept.layer.exampl: Example: with the "Movies" directory selected, layer = 1 matches every subfolder under "Movies".
helpCenter.pathMark.concept.regex.name: Regular Expression
helpCenter.pathMark.concept.regex.long: Matches the relative path from the selected directory against a regex — ideal when folder names follow a pattern (like "[Author] Title"). Capture groups can also feed dynamic property values or library names.
helpCenter.pathMark.concept.regex.exampl: Example: \[(.+?)\] extracts "Eiichiro Oda" from "[Eiichiro Oda] One Piece".
helpCenter.pathMark.concept.matchMode.lo: Decides how a mark finds its matches: layer mode matches by directory depth and is simple and intuitive; regex mode matches by path pattern and is more flexible. To select just the current path, use layer = 0.
helpCenter.pathMark.concept.applyScope.s: Matched item only, or its children too
helpCenter.pathMark.concept.applyScope.l: "Matched only": the resource path must equal the matched item exactly. "Matched and subdirectories": the matched item and anything inside it are affected. Use the latter to tag an entire folder at once.
helpCenter.pathMark.concept.applyScope.e: Example: configure "Status = Completed" on the "Completed" directory with "matched and subdirectories" — every resource inside gets the status.
helpCenter.pathMark.concept.dynamicValue: Property values / library names extracted from paths

Besides fixed values, property and media library marks can extract values dynamically: take a folder name at a given layer, or capture part of the path with a regex group. When folder names change, values follow after the next sync.
Example: property "Artist" dynamically taking the layer-1 folder name turns "Music/Joe Hisaishi/Album" into "Artist = Joe Hisaishi".
helpCenter.pathMark.concept.priority.lon: When one path matches several marks, they are processed in ascending priority. Smaller runs first. Usually no adjustment is needed — only when marks affect each other.
helpCenter.pathMark.concept.sync.name: Sync
helpCenter.pathMark.concept.sync.long: Creating or editing a mark doesn't generate data immediately. Sync reads your marks and generates the corresponding resources, property values, and library associations. Auto-sync is on by default (runs after mark changes); when disabled, use the "Pending Sync" button.
helpCenter.pathMark.concept.boundary.lon: When enabled, a resource matched by this mark is terminal — its internal structure is never recognized as more resources by other resource marks. Ideal for disc rips and other folders that should stay whole.
helpCenter.pathMark.concept.scheduledSyn: Give a single mark an expiration; it re-syncs automatically when due. Great for folders whose content keeps changing (e.g. downloads). Too short an interval causes frequent syncs and hurts performance.
helpCenter.pathMark.concept.keepIdentity: When enabled, Bakabase writes a bakabase.json identity file into each resource folder. If the resource path later changes, re-sync finds the original resource through the file and updates its path — ratings, properties, and play history are all preserved.
helpCenter.workflow.whatIs.headline: Chain small steps into automation you can trust
helpCenter.workflow.whatIs.intro: A workflow is a chain: a trigger decides when it runs and what items it starts from, then each activity processes those items one by one — filter out what you don't want, transform what's left, and finally act on it. You build the chain once; running it by hand, on a schedule, or on a folder change is just a different trigger.
helpCenter.workflow.whatIs.diagram.resul: File-renaming chains never touch the disk directly: a run produces a rename plan you review, apply with one click, and can undo afterwards.
helpCenter.workflow.whatIs.parts.title: The Four Kinds of Parts
helpCenter.workflow.whatIs.parts.trigger: When the workflow runs and what items enter the chain: a manual click, a schedule, a watched folder, or an app event like "subscription updated".
Keeps or drops items — e.g. keep only items whose title contains your keywords. What passes continues down the chain.
helpCenter.workflow.whatIs.parts.transfo: Changes items — rewrite a working file name, capture variables from it, expand a directory into its files. Nothing outside the chain changes yet.
Does something real: record a rename plan, enqueue a download, send a notification.
helpCenter.workflow.whatIs.parts.typingN: Every position in the chain knows what kind of item flows through it. The editor only offers activities that can accept the item arriving at that spot, so an ExHentai action can't accidentally end up in a file-renaming chain.
helpCenter.workflow.whatIs.steps.title: How It Works
helpCenter.workflow.whatIs.steps.step1.d: Choose when the workflow runs and configure its source — e.g. which folders a scan covers.
helpCenter.workflow.whatIs.steps.step2.d: Add filters, transforms and actions in order. Each activity shows a summary of its configuration.
helpCenter.workflow.whatIs.steps.step3.d: Run it by hand any time (even while disabled). Every run keeps a record: items in, items out, and what each step did.
helpCenter.workflow.whatIs.twoPhaseNote: Safety first: destructive work is split into two phases. A run only computes and records a plan; you review the diff, exclude lines you don't want, then apply — and applied renames can be undone in one click.
helpCenter.workflow.badge.removeSubGroup: […] wrapping a name from your "sub groups" list
helpCenter.workflow.badge.trimAll: collapse spaces · trim ends · drop empty brackets
helpCenter.workflow.edge.oneToMany: 1 directory → its files (each inherits the captured variables)
helpCenter.workflow.edge.settled: fires after the entry stays quiet for the settle period
helpCenter.workflow.outcome.planPreview: Rename plan → review the diff → apply → undo anytime
helpCenter.workflow.outcome.planAuto: A rename plan appears automatically — you review and apply when convenient
helpCenter.workflow.outcome.queued: Matching items are queued in the downloader
helpCenter.workflow.outcome.notified: A notification appears the moment a task finishes
helpCenter.workflow.examples.intro: Each recipe is a complete workflow you can rebuild in a minute. They are ordered from the first thing everyone does — cleaning one folder's names with a safe preview — up to full automation.
Strip a junk suffix from every file in a folder — without touching the disk until you've seen exactly what will change.
Trigger: pick the folder(s) to scan and what to emit (files, directories, or both).
Modify file name: the same operations as the File Name Modifier page — replace, delete, insert, change case…
Save file name records the change as a plan line. It never renames anything by itself.
Run it → open the rename plan → every change shows as a colored diff. Untick lines you don't want, apply the rest, undo later if you regret it.
helpCenter.workflow.examples.vocabularyC: Strip release-group tags and ad words
Maintain your own word lists once — sub groups, ad slogans — and every cleaning workflow can use them. Matching is exact, contains, or regex.
Remove wrapped segments: deletes "[SubGroup]" when the bracketed text matches your list — brackets included.
Remove matched texts: deletes bare occurrences of ad words anywhere in the name.
Trim leftovers: collapses double spaces and drops empty "[]" pairs the removals left behind.
"[SubGroup] Movie SPONSOR (1080p).mkv" → planned as "Movie.mkv". Word lists live on the Text page and are shared by every workflow.
helpCenter.workflow.examples.crossLevelR: Rename episodes using their season folder
The show's title and season live on the folder; the episode number lives on the file. Variables carry information across levels so one template can combine them.
Capture on the folder name: named groups become variables (title, season) that ride along with the item.
Expand into children: the folder becomes its files — and every file inherits a copy of the captured variables.
Capture on each file name: grab the episode number.
Rebuild from template: combine folder-level and file-level variables; {var:extension} restores the real extension.
"Breaking Bad S01/Breaking.Bad.S01E01.mkv" → planned as "Breaking Bad - S01E01.mkv". Two shows in one scan stay independent — variables never leak between siblings.
helpCenter.workflow.examples.watchAutoCl: Watch a folder; whenever a new file settles (no changes for the settle period — so half-copied files are never touched), the cleaning chain runs on it automatically.
Trigger: pick the watched folder and a settle period (e.g. 30s).
Any cleaning chain works here — word lists, rename operations, templates.
Save file name still only records a plan: automation prepares, you confirm.
Files dropped into Downloads show up minutes later as ready-to-apply rename plans in the run history — nothing is renamed behind your back.
helpCenter.workflow.examples.scheduledCl: The manual scan with an interval: the workflow starts itself when due. Disable the workflow and the schedule pauses with it.
Trigger: same scan configuration as the manual version, plus "run every N minutes" (0 = manual only).
A new run is only started when the previous one has finished — schedules never pile up.
Every morning the run history holds a fresh plan for whatever accumulated yesterday.
helpCenter.workflow.examples.subscriptio: Workflows aren't only about files: any app event can start a chain. Here a subscription update flows through a keyword filter straight into the download queue.
Trigger: fires whenever a subscription check finds new items; optionally limited to specific subscriptions.
Filter by title: keep only items whose title contains any of your keywords.
Enqueue as download: the chain's typing guarantees only compatible items ever reach this action.
New matching releases start downloading on their own; everything else is dropped silently.
helpCenter.workflow.examples.downloadNot: Get notified when a download finishes
The smallest useful workflow: one trigger, one action. Field placeholders like {name} pull values from the item into the message.
Trigger: fires on every completed download task; optionally limited to certain sources.
Send notification: title/body support {field} interpolation from the completed task.
A toast with the task's name the moment it completes — no polling the downloader page.
helpCenter.workflow.concept.trigger.name: Trigger
helpCenter.workflow.concept.trigger.shor: When the workflow runs, and what items enter the chain.
helpCenter.workflow.concept.trigger.long: Every workflow has exactly one trigger. Event triggers (subscription updated, download completed) react to things happening in the app. Filesystem triggers produce entries from disk: the manual scan runs when you click Run, the scheduled scan also runs itself every N minutes, and the directory watch reacts to new entries in a folder. The trigger also defines the item type the chain starts with, which decides which activities can follow.
helpCenter.workflow.concept.trigger.exam: A "manual filesystem scan" over D:/Downloads with depth 1 and target "files" emits one item per file directly inside that folder.
helpCenter.workflow.concept.activity.sho: One step of the chain: Filter, Transform, or Action.
helpCenter.workflow.concept.activity.lon: Activities process items one at a time, in chain order. Filters keep or drop an item. Transforms replace it with a changed copy (a new working name, captured variables) or expand it into several items. Actions cause real effects — record a plan line, enqueue a download, send a notification. Each activity can be set to either skip a failing item or fail the whole run (see Error policy).
helpCenter.workflow.concept.itemType.sho: What kind of thing flows through the chain at each position.
helpCenter.workflow.concept.itemType.lon: Items are typed: a filesystem entry, a subscription item, a search query… The trigger sets the initial type; most activities pass it through, some replace it with a fixed different type. Hover the type pill between two steps in the editor to see the fields the item carries at that position.
helpCenter.workflow.concept.itemType.exa: A filesystem entry carries: path, isDirectory, originalName, workingName. Text activities edit workingName; the disk file is untouched until a plan is applied.
The editor only offers activities that fit the current position.

Every activity declares what it accepts: specific item types, or a capability ("anything with editable text"). While you build the chain, the editor tracks the type at each position and hides or flags incompatible activities; the server enforces the same rule when saving and again while running. Text activities accept by capability, which is why the same trim/remove/capture/template nodes will work on future item types (e.g. gallery titles) without any change.
After "subscription updated", the picker won't offer "Save file name" — a subscription item is not a filesystem entry. Adding an AI transform in between can bridge the types where that makes sense.
helpCenter.workflow.concept.variables.sh: Named values that ride along with each item.
helpCenter.workflow.concept.variables.lo: Each item carries its own variable bag. "Capture variables" writes into it using regex named groups (the group name is the variable name); "Rebuild from template" reads it with {var:name}, with formatters like {var:ep:pad(2)}. Filesystem entries also answer built-in system variables — extension, originalName, parentName — taken from their original disk state. When a directory expands into its children, every child inherits a copy of the parent's bag, so folder-level knowledge reaches file-level steps; siblings never see each other's values.
helpCenter.workflow.concept.variables.ex: Capture "^(?<title>.+) S(?<season>\d+)$" on the folder, expand, capture "E(?<ep>\d+)" on each file, then rebuild with "{var:title} - S{var:season}E{var:ep:pad(2)}.{var:extension}".
helpCenter.workflow.concept.twoPhase.sho: Runs prepare a plan; you confirm before the disk changes.
helpCenter.workflow.concept.twoPhase.lon: "Save file name" compares each item's working name against its original name and records changed ones as plan lines — with built-in defenses (illegal characters sanitized, duplicate targets and over-long paths become conflicts instead of surprises). In the plan panel you review the diff, untick lines, then Apply: renames execute deepest-path-first so renaming a folder can't break its children's pending lines, and every line's status is saved as it happens. Undo replays applied lines in reverse. If the disk changed between preview and apply, the affected line fails with a reason and the rest continue.
helpCenter.workflow.concept.twoPhase.exa: 200 planned renames, one file got taken by another program in the meantime: 199 apply, 1 shows "target name is now taken", nothing aborts, and all 199 can still be undone.
helpCenter.workflow.concept.automation.s: Workflows that start themselves — on the clock or on folder changes.
helpCenter.workflow.concept.automation.l: The scheduled scan runs its workflow every N minutes (only while the workflow is enabled, and never while a previous run is still going). The directory watch keeps an eye on chosen folders and fires for entries that have stayed unchanged for a settle period — so files still being copied are never picked up. Both produce completely normal runs: same chain, same run history, same plans awaiting your confirmation.
helpCenter.workflow.concept.automation.e: Watch "D:/Downloads" with a 30s settle and an mkv-only filter: each finished download appears as a ready-to-review rename plan.
helpCenter.workflow.concept.manualRun.sh: Run any workflow now — even while it is disabled.
helpCenter.workflow.concept.manualRun.lo: The Run button starts the workflow immediately, ignoring the enabled switch and the trigger's filter — being disabled is exactly when you are still building it and most need to try it. For event triggers, a manual run asks you for a stand-in payload (the editor pre-fills a skeleton); filesystem triggers need nothing since their configuration already says what to scan.
Per activity: skip a failing item, or fail the whole run.

Each activity chooses what a failing item means. "Skip" drops that item and continues with the rest — right for optional enrichment. "Fail" stops the run — right when a failure means the result would be wrong. One exception is deliberate: a broken configuration (unparseable settings, a deleted word list) always fails the run even under Skip, because it would otherwise silently misprocess every single item.
A capture set to "treat a miss as failure" with the step on Skip: files without an episode number are dropped from the run and counted, the rest are renamed.
helpCenter.workflow.concept.runs.name: Run history
helpCenter.workflow.concept.runs.short: Every run keeps its funnel: items in, items out, per step.
helpCenter.workflow.concept.runs.long: Open a workflow's run history to see each run's status, duration, input/output counts and a per-step funnel — how many items entered and left every step, including 1→N expansions and skipped failures. For file-renaming chains the plan panel is reachable from here too, in read-only form for finished business and interactive form when there is something to confirm.
